results.name: medium-mstp-access-root-baseline
results.title: Baseline · MSTP, access switch as root
results.action: Reset the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on both MLAG peers and 0x0000 on the access switch. Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 and both bypass directions and read back bridge, MLAG, RSTP and LACP state. No fault is applied.

host_table.status: not available: no fault was executed, so there is no recovery window

phases.name: Baseline
phases.expected: The access switch has the lowest bridge priority (0x0000), so every bridge elects it as RSTP root with root ID 0x0000.02:00:00:21:00:13. The connected MLAG peers present one shared bridge ID toward it. The non-edge MLAG bond access-uplink and all VLAN 110 ports forward, and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

results.title: One-way calibration · MSTP, access switch as root
results.action: After the RSTP access-root bridge reset and baseline gate, the runner adds a tc ingress filter on host 2's eth3 that drops bypass-forward echo requests (stream 301) for 2 s. It then removes the filter and observes 3 s of settling and a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: One-way bypass cut
phases.expected: The filter drops only stream 301's echo requests at host 2's bypass port, outside the MLAG fabric. Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

results.name: medium-mstp-access-root-reboot-secondary
results.title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, MSTP, access switch as root
results.action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on CHR 1 and CHR 2 and 0x0000 on the access switch. It requires a loss-free baseline with the access switch as root (0x0000.02:00:00:21:00:13). It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: Secondary down
phases.expected: CHR 1 keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch keeps its LACP partner and stays RSTP root. The MLAG pair keeps access-uplink as its forwarding root port. The virtual links keep carrier, so the access switch and traffic host 2 drop their member to CHR 2 at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s), with brief loss on traffic hashed to it.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The access switch stays root, and CHR 2's non-edge access-uplink must reach forwarding without a further outage.

phases.name: Primary down
phases.expected: CHR 2 reverts its MLAG bonds to its own LACP system ID and the access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP, with brief loss. The access switch must stay RSTP root, and CHR 2's access-uplink must keep forwarding as root port.

phases.name: Primary back
phases.expected: CHR 1 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), rejoins as MLAG primary and restores the shared system ID, and partners renegotiate LACP with brief loss. The access switch stays root, and access-uplink must return to forwarding on both MLAG peers.
